retrieval_skill.name: regime_aware_telemetry_validation
retrieval_skill.description: Separate unreliable observations from genuine system dynamics, then characterize the validated post-intervention regime using authoritative logs and latent-process evidence.
retrieval_skill.applicability: When historical anomalies or instrumentation failures may contaminate a time-series forecast and a later intervention may have established a new regime.
retrieval_skill.query_strategy: Search provenance-bearing operational records for the anomaly interval, telemetry reliability assessments, intervention details, and validated behavior across the forecast window; organize findings by observation quality, regime state, and latent process.
retrieval_skill.verification_rule: Treat anomalous readings as dynamics only when reliable source evidence supports that interpretation; require provenance and temporal alignment for claims about the active regime, preserve exact quotations when used, and do not extrapolate evidence beyond its documented window.

decision_skill.name: validated_detrended_seasonal_override
decision_skill.description: Use a detrended phase-based seasonal template when recent complete cycles show consistent drift, stable phase differences, and superior rolling-origin forecast accuracy.
decision_skill.applicability: When a series has repeating seasonal structure plus a modest cycle-level shift and enough complete recent cycles for robust phase estimation and backtesting.
decision_skill.decision_rule: Estimate recent cycle drift robustly, remove it before forming a phase template, restore only the validated shift component, and select this override only if rolling-origin evaluation beats the parent forecast on the target metric while remaining stable across folds.
decision_skill.failure_condition: Do not use when cycle alignment is uncertain, drift is inconsistent or highly dispersed, too few complete cycles exist, telemetry is unvalidated, or rolling-origin tests fail to show a robust advantage over the parent model.
